data.description:
Addendum to existing finding #77. That entry establishes a specific June 21 AIHW medicine-data retrieval/calculation result; this entry adds earlier and broader parameter-discovery, export-trial and failed-exploit evidence. It does not replace or negate the recovered calculation.

June 17–21, 2026 UTC records show custom programs using scanner-hosted pages to inspect Australian Institute of Health and Welfare Tableau dashboards, discover parameter names and attempt chart, worksheet and file exports. This is an Australian national-government target. It combines distinct outcomes rather than treating all requests as successful extraction.

Two June 18 urlscan captures preserve executing programs that enumerate Tableau objects and request worksheet/parameter data. Their recorded eight worksheet requests and one parameter-model request all return 403, with a verified 48-byte JSON PermissionDeniedException response. A later review of 1,238 delivered AIHW private/restricted URLQuery reports adds callback evidence for successful parameter discovery: Measures and LGA VIC values and allowed options are copied into logged callback URLs. That establishes access to specific dashboard parameters/metadata, not protected underlying rows. A separate private program records eight further summary/underlying-data denials. Private/restricted here describes scan visibility, not proof that the target files were confidential.

The same larger cohort records some successful file transport: 216 PDF reports, 74 PNG reports, six XLSX reports, six full-ZIP reports and 58 partial-ZIP responses meet the review's status/MIME/size/hash criteria. The full ZIP metadata also matches earlier public URLQuery reports. Actual file bodies were unavailable in those full-report exports. Different requested filters sometimes return identical hashes; neither a 200 nor a different PDF hash proves the requested filtering took effect. Public-file responses therefore do not establish bypass of worksheet permissions.

Separately, a June 20 URLQuery scan submitted an SVG-handler expression in an AIHW Tableau parameter, intended to change the page title. The request was blocked with 403 and no matching handler execution was preserved. The XSS category applies to this explicit attempt only. Running JavaScript on an intentionally supplied carrier page is not AIHW-origin XSS. No successful XSS, unauthorized dataset access, actor identity or AI-company attribution is established. The cited public reports show representative denial, blocked-XSS and ordinary ZIP-response evidence; they do not expose private report contents or credentials.
data.summary: Addendum to #77: AIHW Tableau parameter discovery, denied worksheet reads and a blocked XSS probe, June 17–21. Broader scan review records file-export outcomes but does not establish protected-row access or XSS success.
